title: Introducing Claude for Manufacturing
summary: Claude for Manufacturing is a plugin for plant teams with 17 skills and connectors to Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365, and Oracle NetSuite. It drafts quotes, quality reports, and supplier requests, and with Infor's separate plugin it can write to Infor, such as releasing POs or rescheduling production, following user permissions. Humans approve work before it goes to customers or suppliers, Claude does not operate equipment, and a Model Hardware Standard research preview aims to standardize equipment settings and safety limits.

title: Using a 'chaos loop' to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requests
summary: Claude Docs, a collaborative editor for people and Claude sessions, launched Sept 16, 2026 on about 50 pods after a roughly two-week chaos loop on staging, where Claude load-tested, read telemetry, and proposed fixes while humans approved hard-to-undo changes. Claude found a ~3 GB memory issue from per-keystroke copying, and copy-on-write cut estimated capacity from 500+ pods to about 50. Results included 4.6M+ docs by Sept 22, about 2B requests with 60 server errors, 629 deploys and no rollbacks, and roughly $125,000 in list-price inference, though the author's $3k-$10k estimate for a small-team stack is unverified.

title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification
summary: About 90% of the Claude Code team's code is written and reviewed by Claude, and verification is what allows many agents to run in parallel. The team prioritizes end-to-end tests on the real app plus property and differential tests, and uses a verify skill, a 39-item diff-triggered reliability checklist, and a REVIEW.md read from the base branch so changes cannot edit their own checks. A commit gate with off/observe/enforce modes is in place, missed bugs become REVIEW.md rules, and flaky tests are root-caused or deleted rather than retried, so humans shift from reading diffs to defining "done" and reviewing evidence.

title: Building always-on agents
summary: Anthropic's guide covers stateful, proactive agents that mostly sleep and wake for brief runs, built from five primitives: event inbox, timers, external memory, permissions/credentials, and outbox. It cites Opus 5.5 costing 78% less per solved task than Opus 5 on a long-horizon coding benchmark, compared with a typical 40% reduction. Recommended practices include treating the inbox as source of truth, running one active worker per inbox, batching events, and starting quiet, with permissions and credentials flagged as the highest-risk area.

title: J. Crew brings its signature approach to styling to life with Claude
summary: Style Advisor, an AI stylist on JCrew.com, builds full outfits for women's and men's styles in the U.S. from an occasion or a starting item, with looks drawn from J.Crew's own photo shoots and refined through conversation. It uses several Claude models: a top-tier model for planning, Claude Code for the prototype, Sonnet as the stylist, and Haiku for quick tasks. The approach is meant to shift online shopping toward inspiration-led browsing while keeping recommendations consistent with J.Crew's styling approach.

title: Your apps can now open in Claude, and Claude can work in them
summary: Partner apps can now open inside Claude beside the chat or full screen, and Claude can edit the live page, row, or file, with the user approving actions as they would for any connector. Tools can be pinned to the sidebar and opened from the + menu without a prompt, rolling out on web and desktop for all plans starting with Asana, Canva, Notion, and Atlassian. Developers can build full apps on the MCP Apps standard, which is in public preview.
